extracted.intended_audience: railroad industry stakeholders, regulatory compliance officers, transportation attorneys, and members of the public interested in FRA rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Final rulemaking document making administrative updates to FRA safety glazing regulations (49 CFR part 223), including revisions to §223.7 (Responsibility) and accompanying regulatory analyses under applicable statutes and executive orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 223.7 Responsibility — civil penalty framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who violates any requirement of this part or causes the violation of any such requirement is subject to a civil penalty of at least the minimum civil monetary penalty and not more than the ordinary maximum civil monetary penalty per violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties may be assessed against individuals only for willful violations. A penalty not to exceed the aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty per violation may be assessed where (1) a grossly negligent violation, or a pattern of repeated violations, has created an imminent hazard of death or injury to persons, or (2) a death or injury has occurred. See 49 CFR part 209, appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which an aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty may be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An aggravated maximum may be assessed where (1) a grossly negligent violation, or a pattern of repeated violations, has created an imminent hazard of death or injury to persons, or (2) a death or injury has occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties against individuals limited to willful violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties may be assessed against individuals only for willful violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-willful violations (e.g., negligence, absent gross negligence meeting aggravated criteria) are not the basis for penalizing individuals under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each day a continuing violation is a separate offense
rubrics_metrics.description: Each day a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplies countable violations by day for enforcement and penalty calculations; see FRA's civil penalty policy for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to statutory penalty amounts in 49 CFR part 209, appendix A
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA will specify statutorily provided civil penalty amounts, updated for inflation, in 49 CFR part 209, appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule replaces specific monetary figures in the regulation with general references (minimum, ordinary maximum, aggravated maximum) and directs readers to part 209, appendix A for current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRA civil penalty policy publication location
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA directs readers to its website for a statement of agency civil penalty policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated website URL is https://railroads.dot.gov/; the rule replaces older references to www.fra.dot.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update redundant/obsolete regulatory text (definition removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove parenthetical in § 223.7 because 'person' is already defined in 49 CFR 223.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant definitions; update cross-references to existing definitions within the part rather than restating.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA grounds for waiving notice-and-comment (5 U.S.C. 553)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedure Act, an agency may waive notice and comment when the action is a rule of agency organization, procedure, or practice (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A)), or when the agency for good cause finds that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the final rule makes miscellaneous, administrative updates (e.g., updating web addresses), FRA determined notice and comment is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866 significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs determined the final rule is not a significant regulatory action under section 3(f) of E.O. 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative, non-burdensome changes that clarify references and direct regulated entities to appropriate CFR cites generally do not constitute a 'significant regulatory action.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 14192 deregulatory action criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 14192 requires that for each new regulatory action, at least ten prior regulations be identified for elimination; implementation guidance defines deregulatory vs regulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An E.O. 14192 'deregulatory action' is defined as an action that has been finalized and has total costs less than zero. FRA expects this final rule to have total costs less than zero and therefore to be considered an E.O. 14192 deregulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) exemption when rule exempt from notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: RFA and E.O. 13272 require an agency to prepare a regulatory flexibility analysis describing effects on small entities; but such analysis is not required when a rule is exempt from notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA determined this rule is exempt from notice-and-comment; therefore, a regulatory flexibility analysis was not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — no new information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule contains no new information collection requirements under the PRA (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520); therefore, OMB submission is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and reporting requirements already in part 223 were previously approved by OMB (Control No. 2130-0525).

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA assessment — categorical exclusion under 23 CFR 771.118(c)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA analyzed the rule for purposes of the National Environmental Policy Act and determined it is categorically excluded pursuant to 23 CFR 771.118(c)(4): 'planning and administrative activities that do not involve or lead directly to construction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is not anticipated to result in any environmental impacts and no unusual or extraordinary circumstances are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism implications (E.O. 13132) — no substantial effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule will not have a substantial effect on the States, the relationship between the national government and the States, or the distribution of power and responsibilities among levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, preparation of a Federalism Assessment is not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule will not result in aggregate expenditures of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) in any one year by State, local, or Indian Tribal governments, or the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, FRA is not required to prepare a written statement under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impact (E.O. 13211) — not a significant energy action
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 13211 requires preparation of a Statement of Energy Effects for any 'significant energy action.' FRA determined this rule is not a 'significant energy action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Statement of Energy Effects required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation (E.O. 13175) — no tribal summary impact statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA evaluated the rule under E.O. 13175 and found it would not have a substantial direct effect on Indian tribes, would not impose substantial direct compliance costs on tribes, and would not preempt tribal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, funding and consultation requirements and a tribal summary impact statement are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: International trade impact / Trade Agreement Act consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trade Agreement Act prohibits Federal agencies from engaging in standards or related activities that create unnecessary obstacles to foreign commerce and requires consideration of international standards where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rulemaking is purely domestic in nature and is not expected to affect trade opportunities for U.S. or foreign firms; legitimate domestic objectives like safety are not considered unnecessary obstacles.
